solutionSql:
SELECT shipment_id,
       event_id,
       seconds_to_next
FROM (
  SELECT e.shipment_id,
         e.id AS event_id,
         e.occurred_at,
         ROUND(
           EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (
             LEAD(e.occurred_at) OVER (PARTITION BY e.shipment_id ORDER BY e.occurred_at, e.id)
             - e.occurred_at
           ))
         )::integer AS seconds_to_next
  FROM shipment_events e
) timed
ORDER BY shipment_id, occurred_at, event_id;

rules.howSolved: ROUND on the numeric EXTRACT(EPOCH) difference, then a cast to integer. Exact .5 gaps are rounded away from zero, but a probe found none in sample, ties or boundary.
LEAD returns NULL for the last scan of each shipment, so the difference and the rounded value are NULL.
The next scan is the LEAD in (occurred_at, id) order. A scan with the same timestamp as the next one therefore gets 0 seconds.

ambiguities: 'The next scan ... occurs after this one' can mean the next scan in the stated (occurred_at, id) order, which I used, or the next scan with a strictly later timestamp. The two readings differ on the same-timestamp pairs only: 24 rows in sample, 98 in ties and 18 in boundary.
notes: Sample returns 678 rows, ties 652, boundary 480. Fractional gaps exist in ties and boundary, so the rounding rule matters there. A correlated next-timestamp formulation gives 0 differences on all three datasets under the (occurred_at, id) reading.
